book.notCommittedBecause: Amazon Digital Services edition (Amazon cover art); the text is public domain but this packaging is not clearly free to redistribute. Keep a local copy with this SHA-256 to run tests that need it.
book.edition: Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice — Calibre conversion of a public-domain edition (cover reads 'A Public Domain Book')
book.structure: 62 spine items (titlepage.xhtml + Pride__Prejudice_split_000..060.html). The NCX has 61 navPoints, 'Chapter 1' -> split_000.html#filepos2884 (a mid-file anchor after a table of contents), 'Chapter n' -> split_(n-1).html. No chapter exceeds 100,000 chars, so split is always 0.

device: Samsung Galaxy S25 (SM-S931B), Android 17, 1080x2340; Moon+ Reader Pro 10.8, automatic Drive sync
display: Baseline and the chapter captures: the user's Moon+ settings — font serif 18.0, line spacing 3, left/right margins 10, top margin 20, bottom margin 16, colour CCCCCC on 000000, portrait 1080x2340. INV1 captures: font 24.0, line spacing 12, left/right margins 60 (others unchanged). INV2 captures: original settings, landscape 2340x1080. Settings were restored afterwards.
notes: Chapter index is an ordinal into Moon+'s chapter list: chapter 0 is everything before the first NCX navPoint (titlepage.xhtml's cover image plus the table of contents at the head of split_000.html, listed by Moon+ under the book title 'Pride & Prejudice'); chapter 1 starts at the #filepos2884 anchor inside split_000.html, not at the file start; chapter n (n>=2) is split_(n-1).html.
Chapter 1 offsets count from the anchor: 'any of them, Mr. Bingle' (ticket 00) is at 1919, against ~1921 from a naive tag-strip of the text after the anchor and ~2603 from the file start.
Chapter 0's .po at its first page is 0@0#1 (not #0): the chapter opens with the cover image.
The chapter heading is part of the chapter text: 'Chapter 2' is at position 0.

A paragraph break is one character in Moon+'s text and is stored as
in the highlighted text.

Invariance: the same text got the same position at the baseline settings, at font 24 / line spacing 12 / margins 60 (INV1) and in landscape (INV2): 'I hope…' 396, the heading 0, 'Mrs. Bennet deigned…' 934, 'Mary wished…' 2508, 'To-morrow fortnight.' 1346 ('morrow' 1349). Highlights made at one setting render on the same words at the others.

The .po offset was the page's first character at the baseline (1993 = 'their chance;') and in landscape (1368 = the quote before 'Aye' at 1369), but at line spacing 12 it was 534 while the page began with 'mother' at 500 (534 is the start of the page's second line).

Lost notes: a highlight created at the same (chapter, split, position) as an existing note can disappear without a *DELETED* record. Seen three times: (a) a heading highlight at 2/0/0 where the bookmark 'Driver bookmark 2' already was — both vanished from the next upload and from Moon+'s list; (b) highlights re-created at 2/0/0 and 2/0/396 while the cloud .an still held *DELETED* records for those positions — gone after the next resume; (c) a highlight re-created at 2/0/934 likewise — exported once, then gone. Once the cloud .an no longer held the *DELETED* records, the same highlights stuck. Likely cause: Moon+ downloads and imports the cloud .an when the reader resumes (opening the dictionary on long-press pauses and resumes it), and the import deletes local notes by (chapter, split, position) (BookDb.importNotesFromText / removeNote's position-only fallback).
Opening the dictionary app from a long-press pauses Moon+, which then syncs to the cloud (the user saw Moon+'s sync toasts): every probe made with the driver causes an intermediate upload.
